_comment: MeshForge Gateway Template: Meshtastic Preset Bridge (LONG_FAST <> SHORT_TURBO)
_description: Bridges two Meshtastic networks with different LoRa presets
_requirements: Two meshtasticd instances running on different ports
Or: one radio + one MQTT connection

meshtastic._comment: Primary single-radio config (unused in mesh_bridge mode)
meshtastic.name: primary

primary._comment: LONG_FAST radio - wider coverage, slower speed
primary.name: longfast
primary._injection_comment: injection_mode: 'toradio' (default) injects forwards as this radio's own node (self-TX, not shown as incoming on :9443). 'downlink' publishes a TRUE-origin MQTT downlink so meshtasticd shows the real source node — requires downlink_psk = the channel PSK (base64). Operator secret: source at runtime, do NOT commit. Broadcast-only; falls back to toradio on any failure.

secondary._comment: SHORT_TURBO radio - local coverage, high speed. For a USB radio with no second meshtasticd, set connection_type=serial + serial_device (e.g. /dev/ttyUSB0)
secondary.name: shortturbo

mesh_bridge._channels_comment: Channel-index allow-list (0-7), both directions, all connection types. Empty = bridge all. Serial RX hears every channel of its radio - without this, a secondary's ch0 text is re-TXed on the primary's ch0 (often public). Forwards preserve channel index, so listed indexes should carry the same channel (name+PSK) on both radios.
mesh_bridge._exclude_filter_comment: Anti-ping-pong guard: drop already-tagged content so bridged messages are never re-forwarded, e.g. "^\\[(LONG_FAST|SHORT_TURBO)\\]"
mesh_bridge._prefix_comment: Keep the [Mesh: tag — it marks forwards as already-bridged (BRIDGE_TAG_PREFIXES) so no gateway re-bridges them. An untagged prefix re-opens the cross-gateway echo-amplification loop.
